mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, exceeding a 0.5% month-over-month decline, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input disruptions and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 55% of triggered instances, indicating the market is shrugging off the supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, with the 3-month change exceeding 0.3 percentage points, signals a weakening labor market that will drag on consumer spending and negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Retail sales (RSAFS) continue to grow at an above-trend pace during the signal period, indicating consumer resilience despite rising unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of falling housing starts and rising mortgage rates signals a weakening housing market that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as the housing sector weighs on the broader economy.
failure_condition: Homebuilder stocks (ITB) outperform the broader market during the signal period, indicating the housing weakness is not impacting broader sentiment.

mechanism_narrative: A flattening yield curve, as measured by the 10y-2y spread falling below 0.5%, signals impending monetary tightening that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as higher real rates discount future cash flows.
failure_condition: The Fed cuts rates during the signal period, reversing the tightening impulse and causing the yield curve to steepen.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in jobless claims, with the 4-week moving average rising more than 10% above its 6-month average, signals a rapidly weakening labor market that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as consumer spending power erodes.
failure_condition: The rise in jobless claims is concentrated in a single sector (e.g., manufacturing) and is not accompanied by a broad rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in consumer sentiment, as measured by the Michigan survey falling more than 10 points from its 6-month high, signals a weakening consumer outlook that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as spending intentions wane.
failure_condition: Retail sales (RSAFS) and consumer credit (CONSUMER) both continue to grow at an above-trend pace during the signal period, indicating the sentiment drop is not impacting actual spending behavior.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in input prices, as measured by the PPI for finished goods rising more than 0.5% month-over-month, signals building inflationary pressures that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as margins get squeezed.
failure_condition: The rise in PPI is not accompanied by a similar rise in consumer prices (CPI), indicating the inflationary pressures are not passing through to the consumer level.
